title.narrative: Technical Assistance Support to Siaya Water Schemes Managed by Maji Milele in collaboration with County Government of Siaya and Dorcas Aid

description.narrative:
In 2018, Maji Milele Ltd. entered into a partnership with Siaya County Government to rehabilitate and manage selected water schemes under the Siaya Water and Sanitation Project. The €2.9 million initiative was co-funded by RVO (50%), Dorcas Netherlands (30%), Siaya County (10%), and Maji Milele (10%), with Maji Milele expected to recover its investment through operational revenues. The support from RVO was anchored under the Sustainable water fund and has been helpful in derisking the investment and also enabling Maji Milele as a private sector operate efficiently. The program is under review for possible continuation.
Operating under a Public Ownership, Private Management (POPM) model, Maji Milele assumed management from local water committees that faced financial and technical challenges. The company initially took over East Uyoma and Naya schemes, later expanding to West Uyoma and Got Matar, collectively serving approximately 110,000 residents.
As a pioneer in prepaid water technology in Kenya, Maji Milele introduced prepaid water ATMs (from the Netherlands) and smart water meters (from China) across the four schemes—enhancing efficiency, accountability, and sustainability.
Service delivery in these communities has significantly improved, now ranking among the best in rural Siaya. Local representatives have strongly endorsed Maji Milele’s continued role as the water service provider, citing improved reliability, transparency, and access to clean water.
Despite the notable successes, Maji Milele has faced several significant challenges in managing the Siaya water schemes. Initially, Non-Revenue Water (NRW) levels were extremely high—over 80%—and despite rehabilitation efforts, they remain above 50% due to old and dilapidated infrastructure, water theft, and occasional vandalism. The rehabilitation budget was also too limited to cover all necessary investments. In addition, power supply from KPLC has been both costly and unreliable, leading to high operational expenses and frequent service interruptions. Another major challenge has been the drilling of new boreholes within Maji Milele’s service area by Members of the County Assembly (MCAs); these boreholes offer water at roughly half the price, reducing demand and revenue for Maji Milele. Finally, water tariffs have remained unchanged since the company’s takeover, even as operational costs continue to rise. Efforts to revise tariffs have been unsuccessful due to regulatory and political hurdles particularly the lack of a Letter of No Objection from the County Government and Sibowasco, which is required for approval by WASREB.
The Embassy’s intervention stems from the recognition that the potential discontinuation of Maji Milele’s operations would have far-reaching social and economic consequences for the communities served. Despite sustained efforts to improve efficiency and maintain high service levels under challenging conditions, Maji Milele has found it increasingly difficult to continue operations due to persistent structural, financial, and regulatory barriers. Consequently, the company was compelled to initiate discussions and eventually announce its intention to withdraw as the service provider.
This decision carries serious implications: over 40 staff members stand to lose their employment, and the reliable water supply for approximately 110,000 residents is at risk of severe disruption or complete collapse in the short term. Furthermore, Maji Milele would be unable to recover its substantial investments in the project.
The Embassy’s involvement is therefore critical to safeguard the continuity of water services, protect livelihoods, and preserve the developmental gains achieved through the Siaya Water and Sanitation Project. This support will be an interim measure allowing the County Government, SIBOWASCO and Maji Milele reach consensus on the operational framework going forward while maintaining service delivery levels.
